title.narrative: Emergency food assistance to conflict affected Lebanese refugees and Syrian returnees in Syria

description.narrative: Syria is experiencing one of the most severe humanitarian crises in the world. Over 12.9 million people are currently facing hunger, including 3.1 million experiencing severe food insecurity. With over 90 percent of the population living below the poverty line, the economic challenges continue to intensify due to conflict, inflation, and a collapsing currency. The humanitarian situation has worsened significantly, with 16.7 million people—three-quarters of the population—now in need of assistance, a number that has grown by 50 percent over the past five years.The recent displacement from Lebanon has further exacerbated the situation, with 562,000 people crossing into Syria since the crisis began. These individuals, many of whom are in desperate need, are being hosted in communities already struggling to cope with severe food shortages. The local capacity to support this influx is limited, given that 7.2 million people are already internally displaced within Syria, the second-highest figure globally. The sudden arrival of displaced families is placing additional strain on host communities and humanitarian resources. It is estimated that Syrian nationals make up 63 percent of those arriving in Syria, while the remaining 37 percent are Lebanese and other nationals. In response to the Lebanon displacement crisis, WFP has scaled up its emergency food assistance and is actively working with partners to address the evolving needs. The WFP response strategy is time-bound and linked to the Inter-Agency Appeal timeline, covering six months from October 2024 to March 2025. It includes three key components in two phases: immediate assistance at the borders, ongoing support in hosting centers, and sustained aid at final destinations. Till date, WFP Syria reached over 320,000 people at the borders and inside Syria. Of these, over 135,000 people were reached at the borders with date bars and fresh meals, while the remaining were assisted at hosting centers, and among host communities, with fresh and hot meals, date bars, RTEs, and food rations.WFP requires USD 54.4 million is sustain this flash emergency operation. However, only USD 6 million contributions have been received. Through generous funding from UN CERF, WFP aims to reach 76,500 persons with life-saving food assistance and 4,000 PLWG with nutrition support over a course of three months. WFP will target displaced families residing in host centres and families/relatives in the initial phase of displacement and host families who are accommodating displaced persons.
